observations:
Torah #219 is a short, densely focused teaching organized around two thematic clusters that are already captured by the two identified packages. A thorough reading of the source text for additional independent bechina domains yields no candidates beyond those already assigned.

The Torah's argument moves through three moments:
1. God clothed His gaavah (pride/glory) in tzimtzum in order to reveal His Malkhut — and this is what destroyed the Temple when Israel sinned and He removed that garment (eitza: gaavah → tzimtzum → Malkhut revelation; removal → destruction).
2. Yirah is bechina Malkhut, and Malkhut is bechina hakhna'ah — because Malkhut has no independent substance, only relational existence (Package 2).
3. When a person hides/humbles himself, God reveals Himself in the mode of 'לא' which is bechina ayin va'efes, bechina anavah v'shiplut (Package 1).

The concept of גאוה (divine glory/pride) appears as the central eitza-actor — it is that which is clothed, concealed, or revealed — but it is never equated via bechina language to any other concept. It is a structural causal concept, not a bechina node. Adding it as a package would require inserting an eitza connection, which violates the bechina-only rule for packages.

The concept of צִמְצוּם (divine self-constriction/contraction) is mentioned but only as the mechanism (eitza) of how gaavah is clothed, not as a concept equated via bechina to others.

The concept of גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ (the verse 'Hashem reigns, He has clothed Himself with grandeur') is used as a proof-text throughout but is not equated to another concept-node via bechina language — it is the scriptural label for the entire phenomenon.

There are therefore exactly 2 packages in Torah #219, no more. The good/evil mirror is incomplete at the package level — gaavah functions as the evil counterforce but has no bechina cluster of its own in this Torah. This is consistent with the Torah's brevity and its nature as a series of closely related oral teachings recorded together.
